title: Why Can't Some People SNAP Their Fingers? 🫰
description:
Snap your fingers. Now snap with your fingertips barely touching. Fizzled? A snap is a tiny catapult. Your thumb presses on your middle finger, the grip of your squishy fingertips holds it while your muscles load it up, then it slips and the finger slams into your palm in about 7 milliseconds: that slap is the sound. Barely touching loads almost nothing, so it fizzles. A 2021 Georgia Tech study filmed snaps at high speed: the fastest speed-up ever measured in a human body, almost three times a pro pitcher's arm. With metal thimbles (no squish) the snaps were more than three times slower. Can you snap? Yes or no?
